description: Review the architecture of a distributed caching system.
recommendation: All engineering gates passed. Ready for human review and approval.

result.response:
Strengths
- Horizontal scalability via partitioning (e.g., consistent hashing) and node auto-discovery.
- Replication for high availability and fast failover; TTL-based eviction supports freshness.
- Client-side load balancing and backoff/retries reduce server hot spots.
- Pluggable write strategies (write-through/around/back) and serialization formats.

Weaknesses
- Eventual consistency under partitions; no quorum or fencing → stale/dirty reads possible.
- Cache stampede risk on expirations; limited request coalescing/locking.
- Hot-key amplification and uneven shard load; rebalancing may trigger thundering herd/warmup storms.
- Insufficient multi-tenant isolation and rate limiting; limited end-to-end SLOs and tracing.
- Security posture unclear (mTLS, ACLs, at-rest encryption).

Recommendations
1) Strengthen consistency and failover:
   - Use quorum reads/writes with versioning (e.g., vector clocks) and fencing tokens.
   - Implement deterministic leader election and fast replica promotion; add split-brain protection.

2) Mitigate stampedes and hot keys:
   - Add request coalescing/single-flight, jittered/soft TTLs with background refresh, negative caching.
   - Detect hot keys; apply adaptive replication, local caching, or per-key rate limiting.

3) Improve operability and safety:
   - End-to-end SLOs with RED/USE metrics, distributed tracing, and per-tenant quotas.
   - Safe rebalancing with progressive migration and prewarming; autoscaling with headroom.
   - Enforce mTLS, fine-grained ACLs, encryption at rest, and secure default configs.
